Land-use characteristics in the plans were assessed and the effect of the Lincoln Highway improvement was considered. The alternate alignments proposed for this improvement will produce no need for changes in the existing plans. Land-use patterns outlined by the plans were presently being developed and the proposed improvement will assist the full implementation of the plans.
Alignment B was laid out in an attempt to minimize the disruption to existing land use by shifting the centerline for the improvement away from the built-up side of the existing roadway in those areas where one side of the right-of-way was open and undeveloped. During the course of the study, however, subdivisions were created and development took place that mitigated the opportunities sought by this alignment.
Alignment A was designed to place the proposed new centerline generally along the existing centerline, and therefore necessitates comparable takings along both sides of the existing roadway. These required takings, however, are approximately one-half as wide as those that would be needed under the concept of Line B. Alignment A, therefore, diminishes the width of takings to a point which permits, in most cases, the existing development along the roadway to continue in use.
As the study progressed, Alignment B was dropped on the basis that it was no longer a feasible alternate due to the development that had occured along the route. Alignment A was the only one presented at the public hearing.
Therefore, the recommended alternative is "To Improve This Highway Facility" in accordance with Alignment "A" which is considered the most feasible and prudent alternate.
